chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The people of two religions do not settle together in one village."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on people of different religions living together in one village according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on inheritance of differing faiths, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a principle of religious distinctiveness in communal living. It reflects the jurisprudential view that maintaining separate religious identities is preserved by avoiding mixed residential zones, a ruling often discussed in the context of *dhimmi* settlements and urban planning in early Islamic society. This emphasizes not just legal separation but the preservation of communal religious integrity and identity.
